title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Seriously Implementing the Arbitration Law and Enforcing Arbitration Awards in Accordance with the Law
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Earnest Implementation of the Arbitration Law and the Lawful Enforcement of Arbitral Awards

Fa Fa [1995] No. 21

High People's Courts of All Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government:

The Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Arbitration Law) was adopted at the Ninth Session of the Standing Committee of the Eighth National People's Congress on August 31, 1994, and shall come into effect as of September 1 of this year. According to the provisions of Article 79 of the Arbitration Law, existing arbitration institutions established by the administrative departments for industry and commerce, urban construction, science and technology, and other departments of the State Council, provincial, autonomous region, and autonomous prefecture people's governments, as well as county people's governments, shall be terminated as of September 1 of this year; existing arbitration institutions located in municipalities directly under the central government, cities where provincial and autonomous region people's governments are located, and other cities divided into districts, and which are currently subordinate to administrative departments, shall be terminated by September 1 of the next year at the latest. In order to ensure the implementation of the Arbitration Law and to enforce arbitral awards fairly and promptly, the following notice is hereby given:

1. As of September 1 of this year, people's courts at all levels shall strictly implement the Arbitration Law and, in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law, the Economic Contract Law, and the provisions of the 1958 Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards to which China has acceded, shall conscientiously handle each case submitted to the people's court for a ruling, an application for setting aside or enforcement of an arbitral award, and shall truly ensure strict enforcement of the law.

2. Pursuant to the Notice on Further Efforts to Reorganize and Establish Arbitration Institutions (Guo Ban Fa [1995] No. 38), cases accepted by existing arbitration institutions prior to their lawful termination shall have an arbitral award rendered within six months from the date of their lawful termination. Therefore, if an arbitration institution submits a party's application for property preservation to a people's court during this period, the people's court shall render a ruling in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, either accepting or dismissing the application; if an arbitration institution renders an award or a mediation statement in accordance with the arbitration procedure during this period, and one party fails to perform it, while the other party applies to a people's court for enforcement in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, the people's court receiving the application shall enforce it. However, if the respondent provides evidence that the award falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 217, paragraph 2, or Article 260, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law, or if a party provides evidence that the award falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 260, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law or Article 58 of the Arbitration Law, the people's court shall render a ruling of refusal of enforcement or setting aside the award, as the case may be. If one party applies for enforcement while the other party applies to set aside the award, the people's court shall rule to suspend enforcement.

October 4, 1995
